intro.title: The Brass Charter
paragraphs: To the Chief Engineer of the {colony} Expedition.

By resolution of the Board of the Meridian Steam Company, you are entrusted with Steamforge No. 9, one of the twelve sealed pressure engines cast at our Ashcombe works, and with the families who have chosen to follow it north beyond the last railhead.

Past the Hollowmere ranges lies country no surveyor has walked. The Board requires a colony there, self-sufficient within the decade, as proof that brass and steam can master any frontier. Eleven forges have gone before yours. Four still answer our telegrams.

The Steamforge will shelter your people and keep a fire against the cold. It raises a modest head of steam for the homes and workshops built against its flanks or reached by a duct, but it cannot feed you, and it will not burn without fuel. Gather timber and stone, raise homes before the first frost, and set your engineers to work at the drafting table: every pipe you lay and every engine you raise brings {colony} closer to standing on its own.
Our supply airships will call when the winds allow. Do not count on them.
The Board expects reports. We expect results.
intro.signature: Cornelius Vane, Secretary to the Board, Meridian Steam Company

dispatches.title: Dispatch: On the Drafting Office
dispatches.text: The Board notes that {colony} has raised a drafting office. Our engineers in Ashcombe have sent the patterns we could spare. Choose your research with care: a colony that builds engines before it can feed itself does not survive its second winter.

dispatches.title: Dispatch: The First Winter
dispatches.text: Word has reached Ashcombe that {colony} has come through its first winter. Three of the forges sent out before yours did not. The Board has entered your name in the ledger of active colonies. Do not make us strike it out.

dispatches.title: Dispatch: Pressure Piping
dispatches.text: So you have learned to rivet a proper main. A brick duct loses a third of its steam in ten yards; iron keeps it. Mind your mains all the same: a burst pipe in a cold month has emptied more than one colony. Keep your homes close to the boilers, keep a stock of iron for repairs, and remember that every house and workshop on a main shares what the boilers can give.

dispatches.title: Dispatch: Feedwater
dispatches.text: A boiler without water is a bomb, Chief Engineer, and the Board has lost two forges to men who forgot it. Lay your water mains before your boiler houses, and build them near the river if you can: a pump house on the shore lifts more than any number of windpumps.

dispatches.title: Dispatch: The First Boiler House
dispatches.text: A boiler house in {colony}! The Steamforge was only ever meant to light the first fires. Feed your boilers coal and keep a stoker beside them, and your workshops will run day and night. The Board has authorised one additional supply flight in recognition.

dispatches.title: Dispatch: A Growing Town
dispatches.text: Forty souls! {colony} is no longer an outpost but a town. Families in the southern provinces have begun to ask about passage north. Build homes, and they will come.

dispatches.title: Dispatch: On Galvanism
dispatches.text: Some on the Board are uneasy about galvanism. Let them be uneasy. Copper conduits carry power where no steam main can reach, and a dynamo turns steam into current with very little loss. Build your dynamo beside a strong boiler house.

dispatches.title: Dispatch: Five Years On
dispatches.text: Five years since Steamforge No. 9 left the Ashcombe yards. The Board would like to see an analytical engine running in {colony} before the decade is out. Only then will the charter be considered fulfilled.

dispatches.title: Dispatch: On Coal Smoke
dispatches.text: Our physicians report that the smoke of {colony} can be seen from the ridge forty miles south. The Board is not sentimental about smoke; smoke is industry. But a colony that coughs does not work. Mind where your chimneys stand and which way the wind blows, keep your homes upwind of your furnaces, and do not fell every tree that stands between them.

dispatches.title: Dispatch: On the Guilds
dispatches.text: The Board hears that {colony} has given its guilds a hall. Mind them, Chief Engineer. The Brotherhood brought Forge No. 11 to a standstill over a single clockwork stoker, and the Board would rather not hear of it twice. Feed them, keep them warm, keep the smoke off them, and answer their petitions; they will work for you like no machine can.

dispatches.title: Dispatch: The Mooring Mast
dispatches.text: A mooring mast at {colony}! The airship Endeavour will call on a regular schedule from now on. Send us your surplus and we will credit the colony fairly, or near enough. Mind that the winches have steam, or the captain will not risk the approach.

dispatches.title: Dispatch: On Automata
dispatches.text: The Board has learned, with some alarm, that {colony} is building automatons. They do not eat and they do not complain, which recommends them. They do run down without coal, and when one seizes up for good it is scrap. Wind them, Chief Engineer, and keep your people fed besides.

dispatches.title: Dispatch: Steam Trams
dispatches.text: Rails in the north! Ashcombe is envious. Keep the tram depot on a healthy steam main; a tram without steam is only a very heavy bench.

dispatches.title: Dispatch: The Charter Fulfilled
dispatches.text: The telegraph from {colony} was confirmed this morning: an analytical engine stands in the north, driven by galvanic power from steam raised in a colony that did not exist a few years ago. The Board declares the Brass Charter fulfilled. The colony is yours, Chief Engineer. Keep it burning.

dispatches.title: Dispatch: The Silent Forges
dispatches.text: Chief Engineer, the Board has decided you may know what it has not said in print. Of the eleven forges sent north before yours, four still answer: Saltmarsh, Brassmoor, Frostgate and Gearholt. The rest fell silent one by one. A telegraph office would put you in touch with the four; an airship yard would let you learn what became of the others. The Board would be grateful for news of either. It would be more grateful still for whatever can be salvaged.

dispatches.title: Dispatch: The Matter of Pressure
dispatches.text: You have read the papers, so there is no use pretending. The sealed engines creep. After a decade at work, a Steamforge's core gains pressure on its own, a little more each month, until it is either let out or lets itself out. Cinderholm and Blackwater are what the second looks like. The Board required self-sufficiency within the decade because it needed every colony able to live without its Steamforge before the Steamforge failed. Yours has begun to creep. You may enjoy the free steam for a while; you may not enjoy it for ever. Retrofit it if you have the plans and the engineers, or vent it and seal it cold. The Board will not tell you which. It is your colony now.

dispatches.title: Telegram: No. 9 Unsealed
dispatches.text: Ashcombe has heard that Steamforge No. 9 has been opened, refitted and lit again under a governor of the colony's own making, and that it runs at more than twice its old head with no creep at all. Not one of the twelve engines has ever been tamed before. The Board sends its compliments, and a request for the drawings. {colony} may name its price.
dispatches.from: Cornelius Vane, Secretary to the Board

dispatches.title: Telegram: No. 9 Sealed Cold
dispatches.text: The Board notes that Steamforge No. 9 has been vented and sealed, and that {colony} now raises every ounce of its steam from boilers of its own. It is the first colony to outlive its engine. Some on the Board call it a waste of a fine machine. The rest of us have seen the crater at Cinderholm.
dispatches.from: Cornelius Vane, Secretary to the Board

dispatches.title: Telegram: The Rupture
dispatches.text: We have the news from {colony}. The Board offers its condolences for those lost, and its admiration that the colony still stands. Cinderholm did not. Raise your boilers, Chief Engineer, and keep the telegraph open: you are not the only colony with a Steamforge, and the others will want to know how you lived.
dispatches.from: Cornelius Vane, Secretary to the Board

dispatches.title: Telegram from Saltmarsh
dispatches.text: Saltmarsh to {colony}. Glad to hear another voice on the wire. We are seven years in, forty souls, and you cannot see the sun for our smoke. The coughing never stops. We will trade what we can for what we need. Stop. Hesketh Moss.

dispatches.title: Telegram from Brassmoor
dispatches.text: Brassmoor sends its greetings to its little sister colony! We are ninety souls, three boiler halls and a Steamforge that runs hotter every season, which is to say free steam for the taking. We have no need of the Company and shall soon have no need of anyone. Still, we are generous. Write when you need advice. Augusta Pell.
dispatches.from: Augusta Pell, Chief Engineer, Forge No. 5

dispatches.title: Telegram from Brassmoor (incomplete)
dispatches.text: Brassmoor to {colony}. The core gauge has gone past its last mark and the valves will not hold it. Pell says it is a fault in the gauge. Stop. We are evacuating the west streets as a precaution. Stop. If you have any notion how to bleed a sealed engine, wire it now, we

dispatches.title: Telegram from Frostgate
dispatches.text: Frostgate to {colony}. Twenty-two living. Coal runs short every winter. We keep a log of the dead. We would rather not add to it. Elspeth Crane.

dispatches.title: Telegram from Gearholt
dispatches.text: Gearholt to {colony}. Forgive the brevity. The Brotherhood has broken our automatons and blocked the pits, and the Institute has locked itself in the drafting office. I have perhaps two months before this town tears itself apart. Do not build too many machines, Chief Engineer, and do not ignore your guilds. Jonas Grieve.

dispatches.title: The Forge Papers: Glimmerdeep
dispatches.text: From the last page of the Glimmerdeep weather log, in a careful hand: 'Minus thirty-one. The coal is gone and the Steamforge banked for the last time this morning. We have burned the drafting tables. Forty years of readings are in this chest, for whoever comes. You will know the winter better than we did.'

dispatches.title: The Forge Papers: Cinderholm
dispatches.text: A gauge log from the Cinderholm boiler office, scorched at the edges. Core pressure rises by a few pounds every month from the eleventh year, with no load to explain it. The last entries: 'Valves at full. Core still rising. Engineer Tull says it cannot be opened without the retrofit drawings, and those are in Ashcombe.' Folded inside is a copy of those drawings: the Forge Core Retrofit.

dispatches.title: The Forge Papers: Ironhollow
dispatches.text: A broadsheet nailed to the burnt guild hall: 'BROTHERS! The Overseer has put a clockwork man in every stokehold. Tonight we take the stokeholds back.' Beneath it, in pencil: 'We did. Then there was no one left who knew how to run the Steamforge, and we left.' The governor from the Steamforge lies in the hall, still bright.

dispatches.title: The Forge Papers: Wending
dispatches.text: A letter left on the Chief Engineer's desk: 'To whoever comes. In our tenth year the core began to creep. The Company told us it was a gauge fault. We did not believe them, and we did not wait to find out. Wending has gone south with everything it could carry. If your gauge begins to climb, do not let anyone tell you it is a fault.'

dispatches.title: The Forge Papers: Blackwater
dispatches.text: From the Blackwater engineer's notebook, recovered from the crater's edge: 'Core up again. Twelfth month running. The valves bleed it and it climbs anyway. We have run high-pressure mains to every corner of town to use the extra steam, and the town has never been warmer. I think we are spending the Steamforge's last years like a legacy.' The notebook also holds the plans for those mains.

dispatches.title: The Forge Papers: Hollowmere Reach
dispatches.text: The Reach answered nobody for six years, and now we know why. Its people never left: they live in the hills above the town, which they gave over to the automatons when the guilds would not work beside them. The machines ran down one by one. In the clockworks lies the master mainspring, still wound.

dispatches.title: The Forge Papers: Lastlight
dispatches.text: Lastlight's apothecary kept a ledger of coughs. It runs for nine years and grows longer every page, until the town fitted copper gauze to its chimneys and the entries thin out. The last page reads: 'Too late for most of us. Take the filters.'
